assessment: The source defines R_c as the apex radius of curvature measured from each best-fitting parabola, defines r as distance from the white dwarf, reports the radial interval 0.4 to 1.4 pc, and gives the log-linear fit log R_c = 0.34 - 1.59 r. The ScienceCard reproduces that relation, its two coefficients, variables, units, Cartesian interval, applicability, and exact global line locators. The executable output remains log_Rc, so the unspecified logarithm base is not used to infer R_c.

issues.detail: The source writes log R_c without specifying the logarithm base. This is non-blocking because the card predicts the reported log_Rc coordinate directly and does not exponentiate it into R_c.
The source marks both radial endpoints with approximation signs; the card uses the printed 0.4 and 1.4 pc values as operational fitted-domain endpoints without asserting greater precision.

controls.definition: Distance of the bow shock from the central white dwarf.
controls.name: r

applicability.statement: The relation is the reported log-linear fit to the observed bow shocks, with R_c measured from the best-fitting parabola.

readouts.definition: Logarithm of the radius of curvature at the bow-shock apex measured from the best-fitting parabola.
readouts.name: log_Rc
